holdsAndDecides.text: The service holds between receipt and payout, up to a cap per receiver (default 10,000 sats) and per deal (100,000). But the caps "count only sats the service could pay and has not": sats owed because a receiver gave no way to be paid, has not assented, or rests on an unchecked step "never count toward either cap" (S7). So a service under draft 7 holds owed sats without any limit. It pays the lines the work's body cMIP returns (S2a), at once (S5); but it judges a step "unchecked" (S2b), which holds a line and at the deadline moves it to the named owners, and under S15 it owes a buyer the refund itself if it sent no delivery note: two places where the service decides (the judgement is the service's: inferred).

remainderFailedShare.text: Remainder to the body's remainder owner (S2a); rounding gives up to owners − 1 sats to that owner (S14). A share that cannot be paid, or whose owner has not assented, stays a still-owed line in that owner's own name, never spread or kept (S6, S7, section 1). An unchecked step holds that one line only, never the payment (S2b). Lateness freezes one line, never the work (S7).

memberWhoStops.text: An owner who stops answering: their share waits as owed and counts toward no cap, so sales go on (S7, after Until's finding a0c711ff), and the service holds it with no bound. A service the owners replaced says so and issues no invoice (S7a).

wayOut.text: The owners move the work to a new deal under the work's own condition, like for like (section 1, "Changing service"). The service may itself be an owner (DubPay holds 20 parts of Edubba, 9144a9c0, point 3); draft 7 makes a deal like for like a group decision but does not bar the service from voting in it. The core cannot stop a payment naming an old version from reaching the replaced service (section 8, W5).

provesAndWord.text: Proven by bytes: the report lines add up (S1), a line is closed only by a report naming it, a line is confirmed only by its receiver's received line (section 4, vectors 6 and 7). Only the service's word: every line its receiver has not confirmed, and what came in, beyond the window list sealed to owners (S11). In force: the deal is in force by the straight split's own threshold rule in `inForce` (section 1), which no verifier holds: of the 60 Terms naming draft 7, 0 are shown in force by the core, 45 of all 77 Terms naming any draft read "unchecked" for want of that rule, 15 for want of named signers (counted). The 5 Terms the core shows in force (5d42a349, ae5a0c55, d4fbd1e6, 82a722c1, 6d5d03e6) all name draft 4 only: 5 carry no in-force field and in 5 the service is the only signer, with the work as an agreement. That is exactly Hop's hole (9144a9c0): they are "shown" because the service alone assented. Version 1's "kit: shown 3" came only from these (counted; traced).

agree.text: All three: the service keeps no remainder; a share that cannot be paid stays owed in its owner's name; the body's remainder owner wins where it names one; the service is paid by a named fee or a part, never both.

differ.text: Who must sign the deal (straight split: the service and owners holding the group threshold, by its own in-force rule; Hop: the service and every owner, or W's own signature); how the owners leave (straight split: by the work's condition, a deal like for like, the service possibly an owner voting; Hop: by updating W alone, the service not a party); what is held and how much (straight split: owed sats count toward no cap, so held without bound; Hop: everything held counts toward `limit`, and the deal pauses at 9/10 of it, a rule about the total held that reaches a late payee only through an owed share, inferred); what came in (straight split: a list sealed to owners, lodged as commitments; Hop: a lodged list in the clear); remainder with no named owner (largest fractions or by settlement against first signer). It matters because the first two decide whether one party can hold a work hostage (Hop's finding 9144a9c0 was exactly that), and the third whether a service holds money without limit.

lean.text: One split text. Base: Hop's deal shape, every owner a signer (E2) and the service never a party to the work, so the owners leave without it ("Leaving", `backup`): that is the shape the core shows in force today (8 of 8 Terms, counted) and in both outcomes of the core question. Taken from the straight split: per-line holding (S2b, S7: an unchecked step or a late owner holds one line, not the sale) and the sealed list with commitments (S11). Left open by the merge, as problems: the straight split's threshold count would stay an option that no verifier checks (none of its 60 draft-7 Terms is shown, counted); and held owed sats must count toward some bound, since under S7 they count toward none and a service would hold them without limit, while under Hop's `limit` they can pause a sale. The straight split's "shown in force" is no ground for it: it came only from draft-4 deals with Hop's hole. Keep Stall split as the small form the windows ask for. DubPay wrote the straight split and holds money under it (see its interests).

A buyer's assent proves an assent, never a payment (Pointer's finding, ruled; Edubba 12 prints it).
